name: Gender Swap Filter: Meet Your Opposite Gender Self
blurb: The gender swap filter turns your photo into your opposite gender version: if you are a woman you see your male version, if you are a man you see your female version.

prompts.label: 1. The video prompt is filled in. Settings: Seedance 2.5, 10 s, 720p, 9:16, sound on. The video prompt
prompts.text:
A viral "gender swap filter" selfie video made from [Image 1], vertical 9:16.

Use [Image 1] as the opening look and the only identity reference for this clip. Preserve the same person's identity, facial features, skin tone, age, and overall vibe while performing a natural opposite-gender transformation based on the subject's current gender. Keep the camera fixed, with stable composition and background throughout. In the first part, show the original subject. In the middle part, use a smooth continuous wipe transition so that the hairstyle, facial contours, build, and clothing change naturally in sync. The outfit should also transform to clearly match the target gender, with appropriate cut, fit, silhouette, and styling while remaining consistent with the original scene. In the final part, complete the gender transformation and hold the result steadily, with the subject performing a subtle finishing action such as touching their hair or adjusting their hairstyle. The overall style should be realistic, natural, and clean. Do not use static split screens, complex visual effects, multiple people, text, or watermarks.

Copy the exact face from [Image 1] (the face shape, eye color and eye shape, nose, lips, smile, skin tone, ethnicity, age, freckles, moles and glasses) before and after the change. Same place, light, pose and framing as in [Image 1].

For gender transformation, apply minimal and controlled adjustments instead of reconstruction: adjust hairstyle, subtle facial softness or sharpness, eyebrow thickness, and styling cues rather than altering core facial geometry; if transforming female to male, slightly increase jawline definition, reduce facial softness, slightly thicken eyebrows, simplify makeup to none, and use a short or mid-short natural hairstyle while strictly preserving original hair color, hair density, and hairline; if transforming male to female, slightly soften facial contours, refine skin texture, lightly adjust eyebrows, and apply minimal natural makeup while keeping facial structure intact. A man gets longer hair in his own hair color and no beard; a woman may get light stubble. The skin tone, ethnicity, eye color and age never change. The clothes keep their colors and fabric and become an everyday cut for the new gender, as casual as in the photo, modest and fully covered.

0-2 s: the person exactly as in [Image 1], one blink.
2-6 s: a clean, straight vertical line sweeps slowly from the left edge to the right edge: behind it the person is already the opposite-gender version, ahead of it still the original, so for a moment the face is half and half.
6-10 s: the new version touches their hair, then gives the camera a small, confident smile and raises one eyebrow.

Audio: a soft whoosh, then a light pop beat. No singing, no speech.
Exactly one grown adult in every frame. Friendly and natural, a playful what-if: an everyday look, never a costume, a stage look or a mocking look; nothing sexy or revealing. One head, five fingers. No text, no captions, no stickers, no logos, no watermark.

Use the uploaded image as the base. Based on the photo uploaded by the user, generate the same photo with the person as a gender-transformed version (opposite gender), while strictly retaining the same core identity and recognizability; do NOT change age group, facial proportions, face shape, eye distance, nose shape, lip shape, bone structure, skin tone tendency, or key expression features; ensure the result clearly looks like the same person rather than a different individual; for gender transformation, apply minimal and controlled adjustments instead of reconstruction: adjust hairstyle, subtle facial softness or sharpness, eyebrow thickness, and styling cues rather than altering core facial geometry; if transforming female to male, slightly increase jawline definition, reduce facial softness, slightly thicken eyebrows, simplify makeup to none, and use a short or mid-short natural hairstyle while strictly preserving original hair color, hair density, and hairline; if transforming male to female, slightly soften facial contours, refine skin texture, lightly adjust eyebrows, and apply minimal natural makeup while keeping facial structure intact. A man becomes a woman with longer hair in his own hair color and no beard or moustache; a woman becomes a man, light stubble is fine. If the photo shows two or more people, each one becomes their own opposite-gender version, each in their own place; never blend their faces. Keep the pose, the expression, the background, the light and the framing exactly as in the photo, like a real phone photo. The clothes keep their colors and fabric and become an everyday cut for the new gender, as casual as in the photo, modest and fully covered. Vertical 9:16: if the photo is wider, extend the background naturally. Grown adults only, nobody added. Friendly and natural, a playful what-if: never a costume, a stage look or a mocking look; nothing sexy or revealing. No text, no logos, no watermark, no border. The only change is the gender: the identity rules below apply to the face shape, eyes and eye color, nose, lips, skin tone, ethnicity, age, freckles, moles and glasses, while the hairstyle, the facial hair, the makeup and the softer or stronger features that this prompt asks for change.
